as_of_rule: a source game is usable iff its (season, week) < the target (season, week): the entire target week is excluded (CFB has week granularity; kickoffs within a week are not ordered)
rule: candidates of team T for target (season, week): players whose MOST RECENT prior appearance (any team, any earlier week) was for T, within T's last 12 completed games, with position in {QB, RB, FB, WR, TE} at that appearance; target-game rows are read only AFTER the candidate set is fixed, to attach labels
non_participants: remain candidates with every outcome = 0; players absent from the candidate set (newcomers / unobservable) are an explicit 'other' mass
historical_proxy_limits: no point-in-time roster / depth chart / injury history (BLOCKED_HISTORICAL_PIT): membership is an appearance-based proxy
a player with no recorded stat line is invisible (no snaps source)
a player who left T in the transfer portal remains a candidate until his recency window lapses (false candidate), measured as non-participation
FBS-vs-FCS player lines are not in the legacy frozen player table: the player universe is FBS-vs-FBS only
forward_contract: forward candidates = timestamped live roster snapshot intersected with the same appearance-history rule; the roster snapshot may ADD candidates, never remove a participant without an explicit out-of-roster record
coverage_2019_2025: actual skill producers inside the candidate set 88.8%-92.0% per season; ~22 candidate rows per team-game; ~40% of candidates participate (computed by cfb_phase1_data.build_candidates; no model involved)
enforcement: tests/test_cfb_phase1.py: mutating any target-game participation row cannot change the candidate set
